summary: The article describes a growing wave of cyber attacks on schools, colleges and universities, driven by the sensitive data they hold and their limited security resources. It cites recent incidents such as the Oakridge International University breach and the Oceanview School District ransomware attack. It then highlights defensive responses: school training programs, curriculum initiatives, the CAEE university alliance, EduSecure's AI firewall, and advocacy by IT leaders.
one_line: Cyber attacks on educational institutions are rising, but training, collaboration, curriculum reform and AI tools are helping schools and universities defend themselves.
key_facts: On October 14, 2023, Oakridge International University reported a severe data breach that compromised the personal information of over 20,000 students and staff.
On November 2, Oceanview School District suffered a ransomware attack that paralyzed its entire network and forced schools to close for two days.
Educational institutions are attractive targets because they store sensitive data, have collaborative environments with less stringent security, and are often underfunded.
Dr. Emily Carter of CyberEduTech says educational institutions are 'treasure troves of data' that often lack the infrastructure to protect themselves.

Lakeview High School's IT department, led by Susan Martinez, deployed a cyber awareness and training program after phishing and malware scares, and by December 17, 2023 had a powerful cyber defense system in place.
St. Teresa's College of Information Technology integrated cyber defense modules into its computer science curriculum, using practical simulations and mentorship from industry experts.
On September 25, 2023, St. Teresa's College repelled a complex series of phishing attempts thanks to its Cybersecurity Student Task Force.
The Cybersecurity Alliance for Educational Excellence (CAEE) was formed on January 15, 2024 and comprises twenty universities that pool know-how and technical resources.
Dr. Samuel Hodges of Midwestern Research University, a CAEE member, says 'Collaboration is our most powerful tool.'
On February 8, 2024, the startup EduSecure launched an adaptive AI-powered firewall designed specifically for educational institutions.
Rolling Meadows School District thwarted a sophisticated cyber attack on March 2, 2024 using EduSecure's firewall, with no data compromise or downtime.
Angela Richardson, IT Director at Valley Tech High School, advocates cybersecurity education reform and has embedded it into every level of the school's academic offerings.
Some suggest legislation may be needed to provide frameworks and support so schools can meet minimum cybersecurity standards.
